subject: baku
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: baku, the dream-eating tapir spirit.
Style: ukiyo-e woodblock print.

spec.name: Baku, Dream-Eating Spirit
spec.description: A tapir-bodied baku with a drooping trunk, ivory tusks, tiger paws, an ox tail and a flame mane. It is built as a stylized ukiyo-e woodblock print: flat indigo, vermilion, cream and ochre, inked contours, scalloped wave bands and layered colour blades.
spec.layout:
The baku stands in a calm, symmetric rest pose, facing +Z, centred on x=0, with all four paws flat on y=0.

SILHOUETTE. A pear-shaped tapir barrel is highest at the rump (back top y~1.43) and slightly lower at the withers (y~1.33). The belly is at y~0.55 and the barrel is about 0.85 m wide. Four sturdy legs ~0.55 m long carry it. A short thick neck rises forward and up to a big wedge-shaped head at y~1.4. The head has an elephant-like proboscis that starts at z~1.5 and hangs forward and then down, ending near z=1.85, y=0.85, with a tiny upward curl at the tip. Two short ivory tusks flank the trunk root. A crest of curling flame-blades runs from between the ears along the neck to the withers. The ox tail leaves the rump at z~-0.98 and sweeps back and up in an S, ending in a flame tuft at about z=-1.6.

PROPORTIONS (push them). The head is large and characterful, with big round rhino/ox eyes. The paws are chunky tiger paws. The mane is bold and tall (to y~1.8). The ears are round.

FRONT TO BACK. Trunk tip (z 1.85), then tusks, face and eyes (z 1.3-1.6), ears and forehead sun-disc (z 1.1-1.35), neck with rope collar (z 0.85-1.15), shoulders and front legs (z~0.55), cream saddle (z 0.3 to -0.4), haunches and hind legs (z~-0.6), rump, tail root (z -0.98), tail tuft (z -1.6).

UKIYO-E LOOK ON EVERY PART.
- Flat colour only. Colour comes in stepped bands, never smooth: a root-to-tip bokashi simulated as 3-4 hard bands (indigoDeep, indigo, indigoLight, skyPale, or vermilionDeep, vermilion, coral, cream).
- A woodblock key-line is made of thin ink (#ink) sweeps of 5-9 mm radius with round caps. They run along silhouette edges: spine line, belly line, leg fronts, ear rims, jaw line, trunk edge. Every flame-blade, ear, tusk and toe is outlined by a slightly larger ink extrude seated just behind it.
- Hairline fur strokes are tiny ink spikes laid in flowing rows. Small gold dots and vermilion tomoe or spiral roundels (karakusa-style curls) sit on shoulders and haunches.
- The saddle's scalloped wave edges (seigaiha half-discs in cream, skyPale and ink) and kasumi mist bands are the print motifs.
- Keep primitives blocky and faceted: 6-10 sides on tubes, few segments on spheres.

parts.builds:
The tapir barrel and its print decoration.

BODY. One smooth loft with a pear cross-section (width x height): rump ~0.8x0.9 at z=-0.7, belly bottom y~0.55, barrel ~0.85x0.78 at z=0, chest ~0.75x0.72 at z=0.65, closing at z~0.95. Skin it to hips, spine1 and spine2. Sectors and bands split the colours by place:
- indigo for the shoulder zone z>0.35 and the haunch zone z<-0.45;
- a cream saddle between z 0.3 and -0.4, covering the back and flanks;
- an indigoDeep underside strip;
- a cream belly line.
The saddle border is a scalloped wave edge made of ~14 half-disc extrudes per side, alternating cream, skyPale and ink-rimmed. These are small seigaiha arcs sticking onto the loft at the two saddle borders (front and back), seated with b.stick on surface hits.

SADDLE PATTERN. On each flank of the saddle, 3 rows of seigaiha concentric ink arcs (thin sweeps in ink and skyPale), 4-5 gold dots, and one vermilion kasumi cloud-band extrude (a wavy-edged strip) low on the side.

KEY-LINES. Thin ink sweeps (r 6-8 mm) follow the dorsal ridge sweep.line(0), the belly sweep.line(180) and a flank line sweep.line(±90) on both shoulder and haunch.

ROUNDELS. On each shoulder (x=±0.4, z~0.5, y~1.1) and each haunch (x=±0.42, z~-0.6, y~1.1), a vermilion spiral or tomoe roundel with an ink outline, built as a spiral-path sweep tapering from 14 mm to 4 mm over 1.25 turns, with a gold dot at the centre.

FUR STROKES. About 40 tiny ink spikes in flowing rows, scattered with a seeded rng over the indigo zones and pointing back and down.

TAIL-ROOT AND CHEST DETAILS. A vermilion chest bib pad below neckBase, and a gold-edged vermilion hip-band with 6 small gold studs round the barrel at z=-0.35.

Colours: indigo, indigoDeep, cream, paperWhite, skyPale, vermilion, vermilionDeep, gold, ink, coral.
parts.attaches: Rides hips, spine1 and spine2. The neck sweep of neckMane enters at neckBase. The legs' upper joints hang at shoulderL/R and haunchL/R, so the leg tops are buried inside the belly of this loft. The tail starts at tailRoot on its rear.

parts.builds:
The neck, the mane and the divine rope collar.

NECK. A thick sweep along neck1 and neck2 from neckBase (r~0.3x0.27) to neckTop (r~0.22), indigo on top with a cream throat strip (sector 125-235 deg) and an ink key-line along the top. Add short ink fur strokes on the sides.

MANE. A crest of overlapping flame-blades, each an extrude with a slight bevel. They run in three staggered rows (centre, and ±0.07 at lower height) from between the ears at z~1.12, y~1.62 back along the nape to the withers at z~0.2, y~1.4. About 12 blades per row, 30-36 in all. Each blade is 0.18-0.34 m long, curls backward and up like a flame or wave crest, and is tallest near the head (top reaches y~1.82). Every blade is a stack of 3-4 same-outline layers shrunk toward the tip, giving the root-to-tip bokashi bands: indigoDeep, indigo, indigoLight, skyPale, with the tip band cream or vermilion on alternate blades. An ink outline layer sits behind each blade. Add a few curled vermilion spiral locks at the base. All blades are rigid on neck1, neck2 or spine2, whichever is nearest.

ROPE COLLAR (shimenawa). Around the mid neck (z~1.0), two twisted straw and paperWhite sweeps wound as a closed loop (r 0.025 each, offset in phase). On it hang 4 zigzag paperWhite shide paper strips (extrude, ink fold lines), a gold bell (sphere r 0.035 plus an ink slit) at the throat, and two vermilion ribbon tails with gold tassel ends.

Colours: indigo, indigoDeep, indigoLight, skyPale, cream, paperWhite, vermilion, vermilionDeep, straw, gold, ink.
parts.attaches: The neck tube starts inside the torso at neckBase and ends at neckTop, inside the back of the skull of the head part. The mane starts at the head's crown (between earBaseL/R) and ends on the torso's withers mount, sitting on both the neck and the torso back.

parts.builds:
The baku's face: the most characterful part, built with the richest detail.

SKULL. A wedge-shaped block of frustumBox and sphere pieces, centred at skullCentre. It is about 0.5 wide, 0.5 tall and 0.55 long, with a high domed forehead, a broad cheek, and an upper snout that tapers toward trunkRoot. It is indigo with a lighter indigoLight forehead plane, ink key-lines on the brow and nose bridge, and cream cheek ruffs of 3 small flame-blades each side.

TRUNK. A sweep from trunkRoot along trunk1-trunk3 to trunkTip: it leaves forward, droops, and ends with a small curl. Radius goes 0.09 to 0.05 to 0.035, with a flat-ish caps end. The colour is indigo on top and coral underside, and 8-9 thin ink ring grooves are spaced along it. Two nostril ellipses (ink) sit at the tip, with a vermilion tip pad and a tiny gold dot.

TUSKS. Two curved ivory tusks (cone sweeps r 0.025 to 0, length 0.16) at x=±0.11 from the upper lip near y~1.18, z~1.5. They point forward-down with a slight outward curve, each with an ink outline and a cream root cuff.

JAW. A separate lower jaw riding jaw, hinged at jawHinge. It is a chunky shallow box and wedge in cream with an ink lip line, set 0.02 m open so a vermilion mouth interior and 2 small ivory fangs show. A beard of 3 cream and paperWhite flame-blades hangs under the chin.

EYES. Big round rhino/ox eyes at x=±0.2, y~1.46, z~1.48, as stacked discs facing outward and forward: an ink outline ring (r 0.085), a paperWhite sclera (r 0.075), a vermilion rim (r 0.06), a gold iris (r 0.05), an ink pupil (r 0.028) and a tiny paperWhite highlight dot. Above each eye a heavy bushy brow of 3 stacked curved ink and indigoDeep blades that sweep up and out, with a vermilion line under the lid. A rose blush patch sits on each cheek.

FOREHEAD. A gold-ringed vermilion sun-disc (mitsudomoe in ink and cream) at foreheadDisc, built from a lathe ring, a disc and 3 tomoe comma extrudes.

EARS. Two round ears riding earL and earR (hinge). Each is a thick ink-outlined extrude disc in indigo with a cream rim band and a coral inner disc, tilted outward ~25 deg. Add whisker lines (long thin ink sweeps) from the muzzle sides.

Colours: indigo, indigoDeep, indigoLight, cream, paperWhite, ivory, vermilion, vermilionDeep, coral, gold, ink, rose.
parts.attaches: The skull back is centred at neckTop and rides head. The trunk root is at trunkRoot and rides trunk1-3. The lower jaw hinges at jawHinge. The ears are at earBaseL/R, and the mane of neckMane starts just behind the forehead disc between the ears.

parts.builds:
All four legs with tiger paws, mirrored left and right with for (const s of [1,-1]).

FRONT LEGS (shoulderL/R at y 0.95 down to pawFront). Each is a tapered sweep over fUpper, fLower and fPaw, r~0.1 at the top to 0.075 at the wrist. The upper part is indigo, continuing the shoulder. At the knee, a cream fur-cuff of 5 small flame-blades is ringed round the leg. The lower leg is ochre with 4-5 tigerBrown and ink tiger-stripe bands, each a thin ring or half-ring sweep. A vermilion thin bracelet ring sits at the wrist.

HIND LEGS (haunchL/R). They have a stouter thigh (r~0.14 tapering), a visible hock bend back (hLower angles slightly back), and a thinner cannon like the front legs' lower part. The upper thigh is indigo with a small vermilion spiral on the outer side. The hock has a cream fur-cuff like the front legs. The lower leg has the same ochre stripes.

PAWS. Each paw is a chunky rounded block about 0.17 wide and 0.2 long, ochre on top and cream underneath, resting flat with its lowest points on y=0 (sink at most 1-2 cm). 4 toes per paw are bumps (spheres r~0.04, 6x4 segments) in a forward row. Each has an ink toe-separating line and a small ivory claw (cone r 0.012, length 0.045, pointing forward-down). A coral pad sits at the heel. Front paws sit at pawFrontL/R, hind paws at pawHindL/R. Ink key-line sweeps run down the front edge of every leg.

Colours: indigo, indigoDeep, ochre, tigerBrown, cream, paperWhite, ivory, vermilion, coral, gold, ink.
parts.attaches: The leg tops sink into the torso belly at shoulderL/R and haunchL/R. Front legs hang from spine2 and hind legs from hips. The paws end on y=0 at the pawFront and pawHind mounts.

parts.builds:
The ox tail and the rump flourishes.

TAIL. A tapering sweep through tail1-tail4 from tailRoot (r 0.07) down to r 0.03. It leaves backward and droops, then swoops up in an S so that it ends near tailTip with the tuft held at y~1.0-1.1. It is indigo with an ink key-line. A gold cuff ring with a vermilion band sits at the root, and 3 skyPale ring bands are spaced along the middle.

TUFT. At the tail end, a fan of 9-11 overlapping flame-blades (extrudes, 0.2-0.3 m long) curl up and back in a spray, each stacked in root-to-tip bokashi bands (vermilionDeep, vermilion, coral, cream), with ink outline layers behind. In the centre sits a larger curling tongue of indigoLight and skyPale. Two small spiral curls frame it.

RUMP CREST. 5 small flame-blades (same style as the mane, 0.12-0.2 m) sit along the rump top near rumpTop and run to the tail root. They are indigoDeep to indigo to skyPale with ink outlines.

KASUMI MIST. Two thin wave-edged kasumi mist bands (extrudes in skyPale and paperWhite with ink outline), draped low across each rear haunch edge where the saddle meets the haunch. Keep them thin, flat to the body, and just a few mm off the surface.

Colours: indigo, indigoDeep, indigoLight, skyPale, cream, paperWhite, vermilion, vermilionDeep, coral, gold, ink.
parts.attaches: The tail root is at tailRoot on the back of the torso and rides tail1-tail4 (parent hips). The rump crest sits on the torso's top at rumpTop and continues toward tailRoot. The mist bands lie on the surface of the haunch.

calls.reasoning:
I'm thinking through the design elements for a baku spirit in ukiyo-e style, considering its traditional chimeric features—elephant trunk, tiger paws, ox tail—alongside classic woodblock print aesthetics like bold outlines and indigo/vermilion palettes.

For the construction, I'm mapping out part groupings: body with tapir patterning, head with trunk/tusks/mane, tiger-pawed legs, and tail/mane flourishes with cloud wisps, plus possible regalia like a shimenawa rope collar and seigaiha-patterned saddle cloth. Now I'm working out the skeleton joints, starting with hip placement to anchor the overall pose.

Continuing the skeleton, I'm chaining spine joints up through chest and neck toward the head, estimating heights for the pear-shaped tapir torso, rump hump, legs, and skull-with-trunk positioning so the trunk droops forward and down naturally.

Continuing the joint hierarchy, I'm adding head, jaw with its hinge point near the cheek, and starting the trunk segments using tentacle-style roles since there's no dedicated trunk category.

Still placing joints...

Still placing leg joints...

Finishing the tail chain with three more segments ending in a flame tuft, giving a total length around 3.5. Now I'm sketching out the mane approach—letting flame tufts ride on neck and spine joints rather than adding separate bones—then starting the parts list with the torso: a pear-shaped body from hips to chest with a dark indigo back and cream belly in an ukiyo-e inspired coat pattern.

I'm thinking through how to fake silhouette outlines using thin ink-colored sweep strokes along the body contour, plus small ink spikes for fur texture, and considering spiral "tomoe" style muscle swirls at the hip and shoulder like in Edo-period lion paintings.

For the head, I'm cataloging the components: the ridged tapir trunk, upper lip, jaw, small tusks, nostrils, and ukiyo-e style round eyes with white sclera, ink pupil, vermilion rim, and gold ring. I'm also planning heavy curved brows, round ears with cream rims, a forehead emblem like a mitsudomoe or gold sun, cheek whiskers, and a wavy beard.

Now I'm deciding how to split the neck, mane, and tail into a separate part from the head and torso to avoid overlapping boxes — this piece would include the neck sweep, flame-shaped mane blades with an indigo-to-vermilion-to-cream gradient along the spine, spiral tufts, and an ox-like tail with a flame tuft, spanning from the neck down to mid-back.

I'm putting the saddle blanket cloth on the torso and folding the tail regalia into its own group—tail, hip flame tuft, and maybe a few swirling dream-cloud wisps around the rump as a nod to the baku's dream motif.

I'm sketching a part budget to stay under 900 total: torso, head, neck mane, legs, and tail roughly split 170/220/150/200/120, landing around 860.

Now I'm settling on an ukiyo-e inspired palette—cream paper tones, Prussian indigo, deep ink, vermilion, beni pink, ochre, moss green, and warm ivory whites.

I'm defining the body color scheme: a Prussian blue base with dark indigo shading, cream saddle and belly, vermilion mane accents, ochre tiger paws with ink stripes, and an indigo tail with a vermilion tuft, then starting to lay out mount positions for hips, chest, and neck base.

Mapping out the remaining joint mounts — head, trunk, jaw, shoulders, tail root, withers, and leg tops — along with torso proportions like centre height and rump taper.

Working out neck and head placement: neck runs from chest top to the skull centre, with the head spanning roughly z 1.0 to 1.85, including the trunk, and height reaching up to about 1.8 once ears and mane are factored in.

Now I'm checking overall width—accounting for ears, mane tuft, tusks, front legs, torso, and shoulder spirals—and landing on about 1.1 for the x dimension, giving a bounding size near [1.1, 1.85, 3.5] with the tail tip around z -1.6 and trunk tip near z 1.85.

Defining torso, neck/mane, and head boxes...

Tail curves up in an S with a flame tuft at the tip, a gold ring cuff at the root, three flame tufts continuing the mane at the rump, and a trailing dream-cloud wisp. For the ukiyo-e styling, I'm planning flat color fields, thin ink key-block outlines, hairline fur strokes, stepped color bands from root to tip as a bokashi substitute, karakusa swirls, small seigaiha wave arcs, kasumi cloud edges, and gold dots — each part builder needs to define its own helper functions independently since they can't share state.

Each part is built by its own function writing into a shared builder, with joints looked up by name through whatever the harness provides. I'm placing a vermilion shoulder spiral on the torso flank, sizing the eyes larger than a real tapir's for dramatic ukiyo-e effect with ivory sclera, vermilion ring, gold iris, ink pupil and heavy ink brow ridge, then laying out the head's trunk, downward-curving ivory tusks, small cream-colored lower jaw, and a closed ink mouth line with a hint of vermilion tongue.

For the mouth I'm leaving a slight rest-pose gap showing vermilion interior and tiny ivory fang teeth, then adding a gold-and-vermilion sun-disc on the forehead, rounded cream-rimmed ears with pink-vermilion inner discs, cream flame-blade beard tufts, ink whisker sweeps on the cheeks, and skipping horns in favor of a flame-crested mane. The neck gets an indigo sweep with a cream belly strip, and the mane itself is built from two rows of backward-curling flame blades running from the head to the withers, each shaded from deep indigo at the root through Prussian and pale blue to a cream tip with an ink outline.

I'm also adding a shimenawa rope collar around the neck with twisted cream/straw strands, four white zigzag shide papers, a gold bell, and red-white tassels to give it a divine-spirit-beast accessory signature. For the legs, I'm designing tapered indigo upper sections with sumi-grey fur cuffs transitioning into ochre tiger-striped lower legs and cream paws with four ink-lined toes and small ivory claws, plus cream flame-tuft cuffs at the wrists and hocks. Torso coloring is shifting to Prussian blue on the back and sides, darkening further below.

Now I'm working out the tapir-inspired saddle pattern: a cream-white band covering the barrel from withers to rump bordered by wavy ink outlines, with indigo dark zones at the front shoulders and rear haunches, and scalloped seigaiha wave arcs plus small clouds decorating the cream saddle. I'm narrowing the palette down to roughly 24 colors, starting with ink, deep indigo, indigo, light indigo, and a pale sky blue.

Finalizing the palette at 18 colors covering cream, paper white, vermilion tones, coral, ochre, gold, ivory, tiger brown, moss, straw, sumi, and rose for blush accents. Now I'm assigning joint roles -- ears as hinges, jaw as jaw, trunk as tentacle, tail as tail, and grouping all leg joints under a shared "leg" role, with upper leg joints parented to the spine or hips and a downward direction vector. I'm structuring the JSON output with parent-first joint ordering and preparing to write the ukiyo-e layout details and mount points.

Writing the floor and mount settings now, making sure only the leg joints touch the floor while the torso rests above it and the tail stays elevated, keeping the total part budget around 870 points under the 900 cap.
